subject: SLA carve-outs requested for content moderation & tool-integration failures

Subject: SLA carve-outs requested for content moderation & tool-integration failures

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the updated contract. Procurement flagged two items we need to get explicit carve-outs for before we can sign: 1) outages or degraded performance caused by customer-supplied content being blocked/filtered by Redwood's safety/moderation layer (our workflows will sometimes send high-volume streams that trip filters), and 2) failures related to tool-integration/function-calls (webhook timeouts, remote tool errors, structured-output parsing failures) that are outside AcmeAI's control but will affect end-to-end latency/availability.

We propose the following: a limited SLA exclusion for incidents where content is blocked due to violations of Redwood policy, and a separate exclusion for third-party toolcall failures (with a requirement to share logs). We attached our suggested redlines to Schedule A. Can you confirm Redwood can accept carve-outs of this nature or provide alternative language that legal will accept?

Jamie

Jamie / Rishi — technical context from SE:

Failure buckets we've observed in production that may look like platform SLA issues but are external or policy-driven:
- Content-moderation-triggered terminations: when an input is flagged by the moderation model, the runtime will reject generation/terminate the request. This appears as a 4xx/blocked response rather than a 5xx.
- Continuous-stream drop when prefix triggers a policy rule mid-stream: partial token delivery can cause increased perceived latency or truncated responses.
- Tool-calling/webhook failures: when a customer-defined external tool times out or returns malformed payloads, the call path can stall and the overall request latency spikes; the runtime will attempt retries but cannot control downstream system availability.
- Structured-output parse failures: our JSON/schema parser will return a structured-error and fall back to raw text or an error state depending on config.

What we can provide as evidence without leaking moderation model internals:
- Request IDs + timestamps + runtime return codes (blocked / moderation_trigger / webhook_timeout / parse_error).
- Sanitized logs that show a moderation decision occurred (flag=true) without showing the moderation signal or internal classifier scores.
- If customer supplies the external tool logs (recommended), we can correlate timestamps to show downstream failure.

Suggested carve-out wording (technical-first draft):
"Redwood's Service Level commitments shall not apply to incidents caused by: (a) requests blocked or terminated due to Customer content triggering Redwood's safety or moderation policies; (b) failures, timeouts, or malformed responses from Customer-provided or third-party tools invoked via the Service's tool-calling/functional interfaces; or (c) failures resulting from Customer-supplied structured-output templates that lead to parse errors. For any such incident, Redwood will provide Request IDs, sanitized runtime return codes, and timestamped logs to facilitate joint triage"

If you want we can tighten the language to be more permissive/less technical — but the list above maps to concrete signals we can produce.

— Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, Jamie Torres <jamie.torres@acmeai.com>
Date: 2026-04-13T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA carve-outs requested for content moderation & tool-integration failures

Jamie / team — legal review and proposed redline attached (SLA_redlines_AcmeAI_v3.pdf). Key points:
- We can accept carve-outs limited to (i) content that materially violates our published Acceptable Use Policy, and (ii) third-party tool failures where Redwood has made commercially reasonable efforts to retry and surface the failure.
- We recommend adding an obligations clause: Customer must preserve and provide relevant downstream tool logs where available and must not attempt to circumvent or reverse-engineer Redwood's moderation signals.
- For transparency, we'll commit to delivering sanitized diagnostic artifacts (request IDs, runtime error codes, timestamped traces) within our normal incident disclosure timelines.

Proposed legal text (clean):
"Notwithstanding any Service Level commitments herein, Redwood shall have no liability, and the Service Level shall not apply, to any Unavailability or degraded performance caused solely by: (1) Customer content that materially contravenes Redwood's published Acceptable Use Policy, or (2) failures of Customer-supplied or third-party tools invoked by the Service, provided Redwood has used commercially reasonable efforts (including retries) to mitigate such failures. Redwood will provide Customer with non-sensitive diagnostic artifacts (e.g., request identifiers, runtime error codes, and timestamps) to support joint investigation"

If that is acceptable, we can incorporate this language into Schedule A and send for signature. If Acme requests broader carve-outs (e.g., every moderation hit), we'll need to escalate.

— Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
From: Jamie Torres <jamie.torres@acmeai.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-13T10:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA carve-outs requested for content moderation & tool-integration failures

Thanks, all — that language is close to what Procurement needs. Two small asks before we sign: (1) please replace "commercially reasonable efforts" with a clearer retry count or time window for tool retries (we'd like to see "3 retries within 30 seconds" as a baseline), and (2) add an explicit commitment that Redwood will not use Customer-provided payloads for model fine-tuning without consent (this is a separate clause but Procurement wants it nearby for clarity).

If you can accept those two changes, I can push this through legal and sign next week. Attaching a sample failure log (toolchain_failure_log_sample.txt) to show the level of detail our infra team will share.

Jamie
Sr. Procurement Manager, AcmeAI
